sections.h2: Which selling routes fit a Rockledge house?
sections.html:
Three paths exist for a Rockledge house: put it on the market, find a buyer yourself, or sell to someone paying cash for the house exactly as you left it. Condition and calendar decide which one fits.

A listing reaches the most people, though you take on repairs, showings and the chance that a buyer's loan collapses. Cash trades a lower price for speed and certainty. All three end with a deed filed at the Brevard County Clerk of Courts and Florida stamp tax on that deed.

Whichever route you take, gather the same basic papers first: your deed, the mortgage payoff letter, the latest tax bill, any survey and the permit records for major work. A buyer, an agent and a title agent will all ask for them.

  • Listing: most exposure, most preparation.
  • Private sale: you manage pricing, showings and contracts.
  • Cash purchase: bought as-is, faster close, often a lower figure.

Rockledge is a city in Brevard County on Florida's Space Coast. It runs its own building department, finance division, code enforcement and public works, so most questions about your address go to one city hall.

Road work near a house can affect showings and buyer traffic. Barton Boulevard roadway improvements are under way, and intersection improvements on Fiske Boulevard are scheduled from April 2026 into fall 2026, so check the city's news page for the street you are on. The city also publishes collection schedules and a special pick-up request form, which is handy when you are clearing a house before a sale.

If a violation has been filed against your address, the code enforcement board is where it gets heard, and the board posts its agendas on the city's agenda center.

For residential permits the city requires a signed and notarized building permit application with a written scope of work, and an owner doing the work personally also files an Owner/Builder Affidavit. Buyers and their inspectors tend to look for permit records on roofs, windows, air conditioning and additions, so it helps to know which of your upgrades were permitted.

Paperwork the building department collects for common jobs
JobPaperwork required
A/C changeoutAHRI certificate, plus a recorded notice of commencement if the job is $15,000 or more
Windows, doors, garage doorsFlorida product approval and installation instructions
Re-roofRe-roof supplement form and deck nailing affidavit
Shed of 200 square feet or moreSigned and sealed engineered drawings
Room additionSite plan or survey, floor plan, sealed engineered plans
Tree removalSeparate tree permit; four trees must remain on the lot

sections.h2: Flood zones and the 50 percent rule
sections.html:
Rockledge treats any development in the floodplain as needing a building permit under Section 30.20 of its Land Development Regulations. For a flood zone determination, call the Building Department at (321) 221-7540, option 2.

The substantial improvement rule matters if you have repaired a damaged house before selling. When the cost of rebuilding, adding to or improving a building equals or exceeds 50 percent of the building's market value, the whole building has to meet new-construction requirements. A damaged house repaired at that level may need to be elevated above the base flood elevation. The property appraiser's assessed value is not used for this test, and an independent appraisal may be required.

  • Ask the building department about open or expired permits on the address before you list.
  • Projects of $5,000 or more need a notice of commencement recorded with the Brevard County Clerk of Courts.
  • If a repair estimate is near half the building's value, talk to the city before you start.

sections.h2: Florida transfer tax on the deed
sections.html:
A Florida deed is taxed at 70 cents for each hundred dollars of price, with any mortgage on the property added into that price. The state holds every signer liable regardless of who agreed to pay, and the clerk takes the tax when the deed is recorded.

Recording adds a few dollars a page under s. 28.24, and your closing statement shows the real total. Giving the house to a relative by quitclaim does not automatically escape the tax, because quitclaims and deeds in lieu are on the taxable list.

The Brevard appraiser sets values as of January 1, and bills come from the tax collector in November. Paying early saves 4 percent that month, down to 1 percent by February, and April 1 begins delinquency.

Homestead filings close March 1. The Brevard appraiser's office has flagged large homestead changes under Amendment 3, so ask that office what they mean for your parcel. Once you sell, the Save Our Homes cap stops following the house and the next owner is assessed at full just value the following January 1.

That is why a buyer's first bill rarely matches the seller's. Avoid quoting your own bill as the buyer's future cost.

sections.h2: What if the house has liens, tenants or an estate attached?
sections.html:
• Behind on the mortgage: once a foreclosure judgment is entered, the clerk auctions the house in 20 to 35 days (s. 45.031). A sale that closes first leaves any equity with you.
  • Renters: ending a monthly tenancy takes 30 days of notice before a period closes (s. 83.57). If the tenant will stay past closing, write that into the contract.
  • Estate: summary administration is open to a small estate, $150,000 outside exempt property or less, and to one where the owner died more than two years ago (s. 735.201). Florida has no estate tax for deaths after 2004.

sections.h2: What to ask the city before listing
sections.html:
Call the building department first, since it holds the permit file for your address. A short list of questions saves a surprise at the inspection stage.

  • Is any permit open, expired or missing a final inspection?
  • Does a tree permit apply? Rockledge requires four trees to remain on the lot after a removal.
  • Does the lot lie in a flood zone, and does the 50 percent improvement rule apply to recent repairs?
  • Was a notice of commencement recorded for work of $5,000 or more?
  • Is there an open code complaint? The city has a code violation complaint form and a code enforcement board that meets on its calendar.

Keep notes as you go: the name of the staff member you spoke with, the date, and what was said about each permit. If a buyer or title agent asks later, you can answer quickly, and a cash buyer will often price the house more firmly when you hand over a clear permit history. Open items do not always block a sale, but they do change who bears the cost of fixing them, so settle that in writing before the contract is signed.

Clearing a house before closing often means bulk trash. The city lets residents request a special pick-up through a form on its site, and its collection schedules page lists regular pickup days.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Rockledge house with an unpermitted addition?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. Buyers and title companies look for permit history, and the city's building department can tell you what is on file for the address. Cash buyers often take unpermitted work as-is, while financed buyers may ask you to resolve it first.

faqs.q: Who records the deed on a Rockledge sale?
faqs.a: The Brevard County Clerk of Courts records it. The clerk also collects documentary stamp tax at recording, and the closing agent usually handles both.

faqs.q: Does the city's 50 percent rule apply if I only repaired a little?
faqs.a: No, it applies when improvement or repair costs equal or exceed 50 percent of the building's market value. Below that threshold the ordinary permit requirements apply. Ask the building department how it measures value for your house.

faqs.q: When is the homestead application due?
faqs.a: Every March 1, filed with the county property appraiser, and the house must be your permanent home by the preceding January 1. Rockledge sits in Brevard County, so the Brevard office takes the application.

faqs.q: Will a cash sale change what I owe in transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. Documentary stamp tax depends on the consideration on the deed, not on how the buyer pays. All parties to the document are liable by statute, and the parties decide in the contract who pays it.
